extraction.experiment: Switching off bias correction with β2 near 1 makes Adam's steps jump to many times the stepsize α. With correction on, every step stays within about α. This is the §3/§5 claim that the uncorrected method takes very large stepsizes.
extraction.reproduce: With bias correction, every step Adam takes stays at or below the stepsize α, even with β2 = 0.9999.
extraction.contrast: Without bias correction and with β2 = 0.9999, the first step is (1−β1)/√(1−β2) = 10 times α, and later steps grow even larger.
